title: Capsule or Tablet: What Actually Decides the Right Format for Your Formula?
summary: Not sure whether to choose capsule contract manufacturing or tablet compression for your formula? NAI breaks down how ingredients, cost, and timeline differ between the two, helping brands pick the right format before committing to a full production run.
body_markdown:
Choosing between a capsule and a tablet feels like a small decision until it starts shaping cost, timeline, and even how well certain ingredients hold up.[Natural Alternatives International (NAI)](https://www.nai-online.com/) works with brands weighing capsule contract manufacturing against tablet production every day, and the right answer usually comes down to the formula itself rather than personal preference. Understanding what drives that decision early can save a brand from a costly reformulation down the road.


## Where Do Capsule and Tablet Manufacturing Processes Genuinely Diverge?


Capsules are filled, not compressed. A two-piece shell holds a powder, granule, or blend, and the manufacturing process centers on precise dosing into that shell rather than applying pressure to a formula.


Tablets go through a compression process instead. Powders are blended, often granulated, then pressed under high pressure into a solid form. This adds steps that capsule production doesn’t require, including binding agents to hold the compressed shape together and, in many cases, an additional coating stage.


These process differences carry real implications for[custom tablet manufacturer selection](https://www.nai-online.com/our-capabilities/why-nai/) . A partner running high-volume compression equipment needs different[quality controls](https://www.nai-online.com/our-capabilities/quality-assurance-testing/) than one focused on capsule filling, since compression introduces variables like tablet hardness and disintegration time that capsules don’t face in the same way.


## Which Ingredients Hold Up Better in a Capsule Versus a Compressed Tablet?


Some ingredients simply behave better in one format than the other. Capsules tend to work well for:


- **Oily or waxy ingredients** that resist compression into a solid tablet
- **Odor-sensitive formulas** , since capsule shells contain smell better than an exposed tablet surface
- **Heat-sensitive compounds** that could degrade under the pressure and friction of compression
- **Larger single-dose formulas** where the fill volume of a capsule offers more flexibility than a tablet’s compressed size limits


Tablets often perform better for:


- **Stable, dry powder blends** that compress cleanly without binding issues
- **Formulas needing extended or delayed release** , since tablet coatings can control how and when the compound is absorbed
- **Products requiring precise scoring** for split dosing
- **High-volume, low-cost production runs** where compression speed offers an efficiency advantage over capsule filling


### A Quick Gut Check for Brands


If a formula includes oils, strong-smelling botanicals, or heat-sensitive actives, capsule contract manufacturing is usually the safer starting point. If the formula is a stable dry blend built for high-speed production, tablet compression tends to be the better fit.


## What Cost and Timeline Differences Are Worth Knowing Before You Pick a Format?


Tablet production often costs less per unit at scale, since compression equipment can run faster once a formula is dialed in. That said, getting to that point can take longer, because tablet formulas frequently require additional development work around binders, disintegration time, and coating before a batch is production-ready.


Capsule production tends to move faster from formula to finished batch, since filling doesn’t require the same level of process tuning that compression does. This can matter for brands working against a launch deadline or testing a new formula before committing to a larger production run.


Working with a partner offering both[high-volume capsule and tablet manufacturing](https://www.nai-online.com/our-capabilities/manufacturing/) under one roof gives a brand room to pilot a format decision without starting over with a new vendor if the first choice doesn’t hold up. Pairing that with[custom supplement formulation](https://www.nai-online.com/our-capabilities/custom-formulation/) support also means format and formula get worked out together instead of the format being locked in before the formula is fully tested.
